analysis: Examined the supplied base_text of ClusterService.swift (lines 911-1536) and the truncated patch excerpt. The visible changes: a new updateWaitLine field; status() now reads value.pairUpdate from a local progress file (ClusterServiceAgent.updateProgressPath under the owner-only service directory, decoded via ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress); checkForUpdate now gates replanning on ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild(pinned:current:), logging a one-time wait line otherwise. These are cluster-onboarding availability/UX controls on the leader. They sit outside the retained threat model's core boundaries (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011); T-041 prefix-cache content was provided but this file is unrelated to the SSD cache tier, so I found no interaction with cache scope, TTL, HMAC lookup names or KEK handling. The gating uses peer-reported runtimeBinarySHA256 facts, which are peer-self-reported, but the existing check already consumed those. The new gate can only delay (not trigger) a replan; a peer that reports a mismatching hash could stall update-driven re-setup, which is a pre-existing trust assumption between paired Macs and not a new regression on the evidence supplied. Open questions for the next pass: the patch excerpt is truncated after the oneBuild guard, so the remaining head lines (974-984, 989) and the implementations of ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress (file parsing bounds, symlink or permission handling of the progress file) and ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild (behavior when a digest is nil, which could let an unknown-hash peer pass or block) were not visible and should be verified. No concrete security regression is established.
